title: About me
paragraphs: I'm self-taught. I started with Delphi in 2006 and have learned every new technology since by getting my hands dirty: from VB6 and .NET to Node.js, the cloud and, now, an MBA in AI Engineering.
Away from the keyboard, I ride track days and play video games. Both teach what the job does: measure before you touch anything, get the details right, and improve one lap at a time.
I want to keep growing as a technical leader, keeping up with how software engineering changes and mentoring the developers on my team.

principles.title: Hands-on
principles.text: Code, pull request reviews and architecture decisions, together with the team.

principles.title: Quality over quantity
principles.text: Automated tests and quality gates before anything reaches production.

principles.title: Simple first
principles.text: The simplest solution that solves the real problem, without over-engineering.

principles.title: Active listening
principles.text: Understand what the business and the stakeholders need before proposing a solution.

principles.title: Focus on what I can change
principles.text: I separate what I control, what I can influence and what is only a concern. The energy goes to the first two; the rest I keep an eye on without letting it stall the team.

principles.title: Mentoring
principles.text: Help every developer on the team grow, with code reviews that teach.
